title: Fix builds when suggested packages unavailable
description:
Vignette builds and `check-depends-only` CI job fail when suggested packages (`vembedr`, `future`) are unavailable. These packages are in `Suggests`, not `Depends`/`Imports`, so they won't be installed during `_R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_=true` builds.

## Changes

- **tests/testthat/test-methods.R**: Added `skip_if_not_installed("future")` to future-related tests
- **vignettes/promises_05b_future_promise.Rmd**: Conditionally evaluate vembedr chunks with `eval = requireNamespace("vembedr", quietly = TRUE)`

## Example

```r
# Before: chunk always executes, fails if vembedr missing
```{r, echo = FALSE}
library(vembedr)
embed_vimeo("505287449")
```

# After: chunk skips gracefully when vembedr unavailable
```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = requireNamespace("vembedr", quietly = TRUE)}
library(vembedr)
embed_vimeo("505287449")
```
```

Pattern aligns with existing `skip_if_not_installed()` usage in `test-zzz-future_promise.R` and `test-otel.R`.

description:
Rename all OpenTelemetry functions to use consistent `otel_span` naming convention instead of the ambiguous `ospan` abbreviation. The new names better reflect their behavior and improve code readability.

## Changes

### Function Renames

All OpenTelemetry functions have been renamed with clear deprecation paths:

- `with_ospan_async()` → `with_otel_span()`
  - Clearer that it's working with OpenTelemetry spans
  - Removes ambiguous "ospan" abbreviation
  - No need to `_async` suffix as there is no corresponding `_sync` or `hybrid_` method

- `with_ospan_promise_domain()` → `with_otel_promise_domain()`
  - Clearer that it's working with OpenTelemetry `{otel}` package
  - Removes ambiguous "ospan" abbreviation

- `local_ospan_promise_domain()` → `local_otel_promise_domain()`
  - Consistent with the new naming convention

### Deprecation Strategy

- Old function names still work but emit deprecation warnings
- All deprecated functions redirect to their new counterparts
- Deprecation warnings specify version 1.5.0 and recommend alternatives
- Comprehensive documentation updates across all files

### Documentation Updates

- All examples updated to use new function names throughout
- CLAUDE.md updated with correct function references
- Extensive inline documentation improvements
- Removed "ospan" from package wordlist, added "otel"

### Test Coverage

- Added snapshot tests for all deprecation warnings
- All existing tests updated to use new function names
- Tests verify both old and new functions work identically during deprecation period

### Internal Changes

- Created new [R/deprecated.R](R/deprecated.R) file to house all deprecated functions
- Updated internal helper functions: `has_ospan_promise_domain()` → `has_otel_span_promise_domain()`
- Updated domain composition to use `.otel_span_promise_domain` flag
- Bumped version to 1.4.0.9001

## Motivation

The abbreviation "ospan" (OpenTelemetry span) was ambiguous and not immediately clear to users. The new naming convention:

1. Uses full "otel" prefix matching the `{otel}` package ecosystem
2. Explicitly includes "span" to clarify what type of OpenTelemetry object is being managed
3. Makes code more self-documenting and easier to understand
4. Creates consistency across all OpenTelemetry-related functions

## Migration Guide

Users should update their code as follows:

```r
# Old names (deprecated)
with_ospan_async("my_span", { ... })
with_ospan_promise_domain({ ... })
local_ospan_promise_domain()

# New names
with_otel_span("my_span", { ... })
with_otel_promise_domain({ ... })
local_otel_promise_domain()
```

title: Implements `wait_for()`
description:
Closes #142, closes #48.

Implements `wait_for()` — a general-purpose function that synchronizes a promise by blocking until it resolves or rejects, then returns the value or raises the original error condition.

## Interrupt behaviour

Chromote's `wait_for()` uses a `synchronize()` function with an interrupt domain that, on Ctrl+C:

1. Catches the interrupt and sets an `interrupted` flag
2. Wraps all promise callbacks to check this flag and short-circuit — preventing new work from being scheduled during cleanup
3. Drains the event loop so cleanup/finally handlers can run
4. Re-raises the interrupt via `tools::pskill()`

This is necessary because chromote communicates with an external Chrome process over WebSocket — pending CDP commands must be cancelled and the connection cleaned up gracefully. The interrupt domain (~100 lines) is implemented in chromote because it requires application-specific cleanup logic (cancelling CDP commands, closing WebSocket connections). A general-purpose `wait_for()` cannot know what cancellation means for an arbitrary promise.

Our `wait_for()` lets the interrupt propagate naturally. This is the correct approach for a general-purpose utility because most promises don't have a meaningful cancel operation — there is no external actor to notify.

title: fix(domains)!: Fix nested reactive domains to be invoked in reverse order
description:
When nesting promise domains, the latest promise domain to be added (innermost) should be the one that wraps the onFulfilled/onRejected most closely. This was happening correctly for `wrapSync`, but not for `wrapOnFulfilled`/`wrapOnRejected`.

The issue was in the `compose_domains` function which was applying domain wrappers in the wrong order. Consider this example:

```r
library(promises)

createVarPromiseDomain <- function(env, name, value) {
  new_promise_domain(
    wrapOnFulfilled = function(onFulfilled) {
      function(...) {
        orig <- env[[name]]
        env[[name]] <- value
        on.exit(env[[name]] <- orig)
        message("Activating ", name, "=", value)
        onFulfilled(...)
      }
    }
  )
}

domain1 <- createVarPromiseDomain(globalenv(), "x", 1)
domain2 <- createVarPromiseDomain(globalenv(), "x", 2)

with_promise_domain(domain1, {
  message("Outer: ", x)  # x = 1
  with_promise_domain(domain2, {
    message("Inner: ", x)  # x = 2
    async_sleep(1) %...>%
      { message("Async: ", x) }  # Should be x = 2, was x = 1
  })
})
```

**Before this fix:**
```
Outer: 1
Inner: 2
Activating x=2
Activating x=1
Async: 1  ❌ Wrong - outer domain took precedence
```

**After this fix:**
```
Outer: 1
Inner: 2
Activating x=1
Activating x=2
Async: 2  ✅ Correct - inner domain takes precedence
```

The fix reverses the wrapping order in `compose_domains` so that the new (innermost) domain wraps the callback first, then the base (outer) domain wraps that result. This ensures that when the callback executes, the innermost domain's state changes are applied last and take precedence.

Added a comprehensive test case to prevent future regressions.

	* then(future) -> as.promise(future); Performs polling for `future` value

* future -> as.promise(future) ; Performs polling
	* resolve(p)
	* then(p)

title: test: Ensure execution order of promise chains
description:
Closes #150.

The final resolution is taken out of the `later::later()` call in this PR. The tests below behave identically before and after this PR.

Revdepcheck cloud check was also run and returned clean.

```r
library(promises)

then(mirai::mirai(1), function(x) stop("outer"))
then(mirai::mirai(stop("inner")), function(x) stop("outer"))
then(mirai::mirai(non), function(x) stop("outer"))
then(mirai::mirai(stop("inner")), function(x) stop("outer"), function(x) stop("rejected"))
then(mirai::mirai(rexp()), function(x) stop("outer"), function(x) print(x))
then(mirai::mirai(TRUE), print)
mirai::mirai(1) |> then(\(x) stop("outer1")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) stop("rejected"))
mirai::mirai(1) |> then(\(x) stop("outer1")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) print(x))
mirai::mirai(stop("inner")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) "rejected") |> then(\(x) stop("really rejected"))
mirai::mirai(stop("inner")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) "rejected") |> then(\(x) print(paste0("not really ", x)))

then(future_promise(1), function(x) stop("outer"))
then(future_promise(stop("inner")), function(x) stop("outer"))
then(future_promise(non), function(x) stop("outer"))
then(future_promise(stop("inner")), function(x) stop("outer"), function(x) stop("rejected"))
then(future_promise(rexp()), function(x) stop("outer"), function(x) print(x))
then(future_promise(TRUE), print)
future_promise(1) |> then(\(x) stop("outer1")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) stop("rejected"))
future_promise(1) |> then(\(x) stop("outer1")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) print(x))
future_promise(stop("inner")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) "rejected") |> then(\(x) stop("really rejected"))
future_promise(stop("inner")) |> then(\(x) stop("resolved"), \(x) "rejected") |> then(\(x) print(paste0("not really ", x)))
```

Importantly, this doesn't affect the expected ordering of callbacks. In the following case 'first' will be printed before 'second':

```r
p <- promise_resolve(NULL)
p$then(function(x) cat("second\n"))
cat("first\n")
```

title: Speed bump for rapid `future_promise()` submissions with limited workers
description:
Found while debugging https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2196

Reprex app:

```r
library(shiny)
library(future)
# Use `promises::future_promise()` to allow other shiny users to be able to compute.
# Recommended to always use `promises::future_promise()` instead of `future::future()`
library(promises)
# Pick a plan that makes sense for your use case.
# For this example, using `multisession` and max workers = 3
future::plan("multisession", workers = 3)

# Temp work around: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/3574
options(shiny.deepstacktrace = FALSE)

ui <- fluidPage(
  sliderInput("slider", "Number of items", min = 100, max = 500, value = 500),
  plotOutput("plot")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    req(input$slider)

    progress <- Progress$new(session)

    progress$set(message = 'Calculation in progress.')

    # Retrieve `input$slider` outside of `future`
    start <- Sys.time()
    prep <- NULL
    n <- input$slider
    seq_len(n) %>%
      lapply(function(i) {
        promises::future_promise({
          # Do heavy computations in a `future` worker
          data.frame(i = i, pid = Sys.getpid())
        }) %>%
          promises::finally(function() {
            if (is.null(prep)) {
              prep <<- Sys.time()
              message("Prep time: ", prep - start)
            }
            # Update progress bar in the main R session
            progress$inc(1/n, detail = paste('Computating...', i))
          })
      }) %>%
      # Wait for all promises to finish. Return single promise.
      promises::promise_all(.list = .) %>%
      promises::then(function(results) {
        # Extract result and plot in main R session
        plot(do.call(rbind, results))
      }) %>% promises::finally(function() {
        # Close the progress bar.

title: Add `wrapOnFinally` to promise domains
description:
This feature adds the ability for promise domains to handle `finally` differently than `resolved`/`rejected`.

When using private event loops to implement synchronous functions on top of promises, we need to take special care to make sure `finally` handlers get called even in the face of R interrupt. We can implement this with a promise domain, but only if promise domains can distinguish between `finally` and regular `resolve`/`reject` semantics. This causes the notion of `finally` to be pushed a little deeper into the promise abstractions, as previously it was literally just syntactic sugar over the regular `then`. Now, `then` has an explicit `onFinally`; though once promise domains encounter the finally handler, we then immediately split the finally into resolve/reject so it doesn't complicate the actual implementation of `doResolve`/`doReject` and friends.

With this PR, you can seamlessly treat regular `future()` results as promises.

```
library(promises)
